@access @access-nl-scope @task-472
Feature:Access Rights — the Objekt's own people maintain its Lieferschein-Vorlage 49s 710ms 2

The Projektmanager and the Vorarbeiter of an Objekt may add and change the
positions of its Lieferschein-Vorlage themselves, on that Objekt only
(task #472). Before, both roles could only read the tab.

End-to-end because this is the access rule as the user experiences it — the
real login, the real project form, the positions dialog and the save that
carries them inside the project — which is the case tests-e2e/CLAUDE.md
names as worth a browser. The grants, the field whitelist, the two write
scopes and the untouched roles are proven at unit level in
wolfinne_ifms_employee_pwa/tests/test_prepared_note_access.py; this feature
checks only what the form adds: that a Vorarbeiter (who had no write right
on the project at all before) can save the tab, and that a Bereichsleiterin
seated as Vorarbeiter on a colleague's Objekt saves it there too. Until the
task 338 decision E28 that second save was refused: the project of an Auftrag is now
managed by the Niederlassungsleiter with the confirming Bereichsleiter as
Vorarbeiter, so the seat counts for the Bereichsleitung as for the
Vorarbeiter role. The refusal on an Objekt the user does not run is
unit-tested.

beide Daten ein" on every Antrag senden. The type select's placeholder was
not the selected option, so the browser displayed the first real type while
the form's state held "nothing chosen". Playwright drives the real form here

open on the placeholder, submitting without a choice must say so, and a

Feature:A forgotten check-out is visible in the Employee App 17s 26ms 3

Task #358: an employee who checked in yesterday and never checked out is
greeted the next morning by "Eingecheckt seit 06:05" with no date and no
warning, and when a new check-in silently closes yesterday's visit the app
says nothing. The server side of both situations (the auto-close at the
planned end, the nightly job, the validation queue) is covered by the Odoo
unit tests of wolfinne_ifms_employee_pwa (TestEmployeePwaForgottenCheckout).
Playwright drives the real app here because what is under test is what the
OWL card and the notice *render* from that payload: the day on the mark,
the warning line once the planned end has passed, the Check-Out button that
must still be there, and the sentence after a check-in that closed a visit.
None of that can be proven by asserting on the JSON the card reads.

@hr @employee-app @regression @task-496
Feature:The Employee App shows a shared device's cache only to the employee it belongs to 48s 582ms 11

Task 496 review: the app keeps its last data and its queued check-ins in
the browser so it starts without a connection, and until #496 that cache
carried no owner. On a device two employees share, the second one booted
into the first one's name and shifts, and their queued taps went out in the
second one's session. Only a browser has that cache, so this is end-to-end:
the app is opened with its API unreachable, which makes it render from the
cache alone. A cache from before the update has no owner recorded and is
matched by the employee's name. Signing out drops the cache, but only once
the server answers: with the connection gone it keeps the employee signed
in with their data rather than half-clearing the device (spec EC-S9). What
a session that ended without Abmelden leaves is cleared at the next
employee's sync, all but the taps it could not send. Those taps, and the
ones another employee left in the cache from before the update, wait for
their owner's next sign-in, oldest first with the employee's own; a queued
tap the server refuses is shown with its reason, and kept for the next
sign-in if the employee signs out before reading it.

Massenlauf as well as posted invoices.

read against the column titles the browser shows.

@planning @task-357 @regression
Feature:Planning Mitarbeiter picker — stepping outside the own hierarchy 9s 843ms 1

A planner may assign any active employee of the company to a shift, but the
Mitarbeiter dialog still opens on their own team so the everyday list stays
short; reaching the rest of the company is a deliberate act.

End-to-end because the behaviour under test is a rendered search state, not a
computed set. Which employees the planner may assign is already proven at the
unit level by test_planning_company_wide_assignment; what no TransactionCase
can observe is that the dialog opens with the Mein Team facet applied, that
removing it is what widens the visible list, and that a name from the widened
list is selectable and lands on the form. That is AC-1 and AC-2.

It deliberately stops at the form. Saving is covered by
test_planning_company_wide_assignment, including the part a browser test
would have to stage an Objekt for: a shift for somebody outside your team on
a project that is not yours is refused by rule_planning_slot_global_scope,
so "it saves" is two rules interacting rather than one rendering.

@planning
Feature:Planning Gantt: the pointer over the shifts while the plan reloads (Task #478 regression) 16s 600ms 2

Reported from Stage and reproduced there again on 2026-11-10, after the first
fix: moving the mouse over the shifts while the plan loads another month opens
"Hoppla! Etwas ist schiefgelaufen", and the view is unusable until the dialog
is closed.

Cause: as soon as the new data is in, core rebuilds the renderer's pill map,
and Owl patches the screen on the next animation frame. A pointer event in
between reaches a shift still drawn from the old data and is answered from the
new map, where its id is missing or names another shift. The hover asks for
the shift's resize handles and, near a day border, for its split tool; a shift
held down when the data arrives would be dragged against the new map.

End-to-end because what breaks is a real pointer against the screen in one
animation frame; no unit test reaches the browser. The frame is held open on
purpose: the page's clock is paused while the next month loads, which stops
animation frames, so Owl cannot patch until the clock runs again. Without
that the window lasts one frame, and a scenario that only moved the mouse
would be green against the unfixed code. Each scenario checks that the
renderer has rebuilt its map while the old month is still drawn. The next
month holds none of the project's shifts, so every old shift's id is missing
from the new map and the unfixed code fails on each one.

@project @task-426 @task-566 @tz-europe-vienna
Feature:Project without an Auftrag, Auftrag anlegen and billing 34s 975ms 3

A Bereichsleitung opens a project before its Auftrag exists, so staff can be
planned at short notice; the Auftrag is created from the project later and
carries its number, and only then is the work billed. The unit suites prove
the rules (test_adhoc_project.py: the number, the fixed Kategorie, the link
at confirmation, one Auftrag per project, the Faktura gate;
test_adhoc_project_access.py: who may create it).

What only a browser shows, and what the task asks to be tried, is the route
as the people meet it: the Projekt app's form, where the Kategorie turns the
name into "Neu" and the save draws the number; the refusal at the phase bar
of the month's task; the Angebot that Auftrag anlegen opens in a dialog with
the project's number, saved there by the Bereichsleitung and linked to the
project; and the invoice Faktura then creates from that Auftrag.

Since #566 the second scenario also walks the Niederlassungsleitung's step:
an ad-hoc Kategorie carries the Verrechnungsart Manuell (#483 D46), and a
Manuell month reaches Faktura from NL Freigabe only. So the confirmed
Auftrag no longer lets the Bereichsleitung release the month herself; she
forwards it with An NL weiterleiten, and the Niederlassungsleitung releases
it. The rule itself is proven by the unit tests
(test_task_manual_nl_freigabe.py); what the scenario adds is that the two
dialogs of that route work for a project opened without an Auftrag.

@project @regression @task-466
Feature:The chatter waits until a user asks for it 7s 695ms 1

The chatter is not rendered on a form view until the user switches it on,
and that choice is theirs alone and is remembered. The server side is a
Boolean on res.users.settings and is unit-tested
(test_chatter_visibility_setting.py, 13 tests): the default, the write
through core's own method, that one user cannot write another's, that the
value reaches the browser, and that a notification mail's View button
names the message it was written for.

What only a browser can show is this scenario: that the panel is absent,
that the switch brings it back, that the next record honours the choice
without touching the switch again, and that it survives a logout. Those
are rendering decisions in OWL across navigation, which constitution
section III names as the case for an E2E test; a unit test can assert the
stored Boolean and nothing about what is on the screen.

Feature:Project phase — Durchführung needs the Kontrollstunden 16s 6ms 2

A month of an Unterhaltsreinigung or Bewachung contract may not be declared
running before the contracted hours are on the record. The gate lives in
project.task.write() and create(), where the unit suite
(test_project_phase_requires_control_hours.py, 27 tests) proves all of its
branches: the two categories, the sub-category, the Objekt without an
Auftrag, the second drag through Blockiert, the create, the ordinary task,
the adoption of a hand-made card, the way back from NL Freigabe, the
elevated write and the weekly digest.

What only a browser shows is what these scenarios are for, and they run as
the **Bereichsleiterin** rather than as admin, because that is the claim:
that the refusal reaches the person who can act on it, as a dialog she can
read, from the phase bar of the form she works in and under her own record
rules — and that the card does not move behind the dialog. A UserError
raised in a unit test proves the rule; it does not prove that the user is
told. Constitution §III asks for this one scenario for a UI-visible fix in
a module the BDD stack installs.

Feature:The first reported hour starts the month's phase 26s 508ms 2

The month's "Tätigkeiten MM/JJJJ" task used to sit in Planung until somebody
moved it by hand. Since #477 the first hour an employee reports moves it to
Durchführung by itself, if the month has Kontrollstunden, and OdooBot says so
on the task; a month born without them stays in Planung with one reminder.
The rule, its gate and its wording are pinned by the unit tests
(test_project_phase_on_first_time_report.py, 22 cases;
test_employee_pwa_phase_on_first_hour.py, 4 cases). What they cannot show is
the real chain: the move runs in a cr.postcommit hook, after the
Mitarbeiter-App's check-out request has committed, in a transaction of its
own, which a TransactionCase only simulates by draining the queue by hand.
So this walks it end to end: a portal employee taps Check-In and Check-Out in
the app, and the Bereichsleiterin reloads the task and reads its phase and
its chatter, in German.

@project @regression @task-481 @tz-europe-vienna
Feature:From an Objekt straight into its Einsatzplanung 7s 113ms 2

Task #481: the project form had no way into Planning at all — a person
reading an Objekt had to leave it, open Einsatzplanung and filter by project
by hand. A smart button now jumps there, on the current month, showing that
Objekt's shifts and nothing else.

Deliberately end-to-end: the unit tests in test_project_planning_button.py
prove everything the server decides — the button, its group gate and the
action's domain and context. What the web client then does with the context
is the whole point of the task and only a browser shows it: `initialDate`
is the single key the Gantt reads (the calendar view's `initial_date` is
dropped without a word), and the range it opens on can be overruled by the
range the client remembers per Gantt view, which it stores on the first
load of every Gantt. So the browser's clock runs a month behind (a Gantt
that ignored `initialDate` would show other months) and the Planning
menu's Gantt remembers "week", as it does for every real planner. And an
Objekt with nothing planned must open on an empty Gantt: whether the client
fills an empty range with its sample shifts is decided in the browser.

Feature:Project task — how many reported times still await release 28s 253ms 3

A Bereichsleiterin opens a month task and sees, as a stat button, how many
reported times on it still need her release; clicking it opens exactly
those, where she releases them. Since #486 (D-K9, E21) the button leads her
to Zeitfreigaben, the one place she releases visits: timesheet lines are
read-only for her role. This is deliberately end-to-end for two reasons the
unit level cannot reach. First, the button has to survive view combination:
project.view_task_form2 is inherited by hr_timesheet, project_enterprise,
timesheet_grid and these modules, and an arch assertion proves only that
the xpath applied, not that the button rendered in the assembled form.
Second, this is an access rule as the user experiences it: after a real
login, the number she gets and the list the click opens are the behaviour
under test. The counting rules, the action's domain and the role test are
unit tests (test_timesheet_validation_indicator.py,
test_employee_pwa_zeiterfassung_consolidation.py); none of that is
re-proven here.

@sale-order @task-332
Feature:Invoice address per Verkaufsauftrag, as each role sees it 19s 105ms 3

Task #332: two orders of one customer may bill to different invoice
addresses, the invoice takes the order's, and Faktura may pick another one on
a draft. The server side — the flag, the constraint, the invoice inheriting
the address, the PDF precedence — is covered by the Odoo unit tests of
wolfinne_ifms_customization (TestInvoiceAddressPerOrder). This feature is
end-to-end because the gap it closes is what a role sees: the field was
hidden behind Odoo's "Kundenadressen" setting and the invoice partner picker
refused address children. Whether Kalkulation now finds a pickable
Rechnungsadresse on the order form and Faktura can choose one on a draft
invoice is an access rule as the user experiences it, which the ORM cannot
show. No read-only scenario: every internal sales role writes sale.order
through the sales-app floor (TASK_SPEC_ACCESS_RIGHTS.md §7.4), so there is
no role that sees the field and may not set it.

Task 503 bounds the invoice partner picker on a draft that bills an order to
that order's customer and its invoice addresses, with nothing under an
Objekt. The bound is a view domain the ORM never applies, so only the
browser shows which addresses Faktura is offered. The Druckadresse it adds,
its precedence and its match with the PDF are covered by
TestInvoiceAddressPerDraft; here only its presence on the form is checked.

with an access error, because the role only reads projects. Now the seeded
services create the project on confirmation, the button works as a process
step for that role, and since the amendment of 2026-10-18 the project is
managed by the Niederlassungsleiter of the order's Niederlassung (the
confirming user when there is none) with the confirming user as Vorarbeiter,
whoever the Vertriebsmitarbeiter is, so the Bereichsleiter finds it.
End-to-end because the smart button and the project list as the
Bereichsleiter sees them are the symptom of the task; the resolution of the
Niederlassungsleiter is unit-tested, and the stack seeds none (spec D-14), so
here the Bereichsleiterin manages the project herself.
Fails before the fix: the project has no manager and the Bereichsleiter cannot
see it (with a product tracking "no", it does not exist at all); under the
rule of 2026-09-07 it belonged to the Vertriebsmitarbeiter, here the
Niederlassungsleiter, and was invisible to her.

product "Hausreinigung" of wolfinne_ifms_data_prod, and signature images on the
Bereichsleiterin's employee and on the Geschaeftsfuehrung signer, because a

@regression @sale-order @task-546
Feature:A customer's reply to the Angebot mail lands in the Angebot 12s 556ms 1

The #200 unit test proves that a reply threads into the Angebot. What it
cannot show is the chatter the Verkäufer then works in: that the reply is
there, and that "Nachricht senden" lists the customer under "An:", which is
decided by the chatter's JS (suggested recipients), not by the ORM. The
customer never becomes a follower (review of PR #778), so this is the only
way a chatter message reaches him.
The reply goes through Odoo's mail gateway with the headers a mail client
sets, so the scenario passes with or without an alias domain, an incoming
server or an outgoing server: it does not depend on the instance's mail
configuration (#546, #547).

nothing is saved on the way, and the quote is still there afterwards.

which no unit test renders. The unit suite asserts the widget and that the
quote's own rules are untouched.

@sale-order @task-468 @tz-europe-vienna
Feature:A new version of an Auftrag, valid from a day, as the form, the list and the PDF show it 7s 186ms 1

Task #468: a confirmed Auftrag gets a new version with the same number, valid
from a Gültig ab; one version is valid on a day, and the one it replaces is
then Abgelöst. The rules themselves (the Gültig ab checks, at most one version
to come, the version state, the Massenlauf and the project) are proven by the
unit tests of wolfinne_ifms_customization (tests/test_quote_versioning.py) and
are not walked again here. This feature is end-to-end for what only the
browser shows: that the header offers "Neue Version" and opens the new
Angebot, that the form shows its number, Version and proposed Gültig ab, that
the "Versionen" smart button lists the versions with the columns Version,
Gültig ab, Gültig bis and Versionsstatus, and that the quotation report
prints the version under the number (TEST_CASES_QUOTE_VERSIONING.md TC-02,
TC-08, TC-10).
Version 1 is arranged as confirmed yesterday: a version valid today must
start after version 1, and a Sonderreinigung Auftrag (Manuell since #483) is
proposed today rather than the 1st of next month.
Requires: fixture property "Testobjekt Wien" linked to IFMS GmbH, the seeded
Kategorie "Sonderreinigung" with a product, and the signers "Administrator"
and "Test Unterzeichner".
